quotes.text: Mist steals certainty, not fruit. Wait for the boat before judging the keeper.
Mist changes what eyes count, not what hands have done.

note: Each round: traveler gives five, keeper returns seven, fog hides fruit, fox says wait; roles swap. No sanction.

quotes.text: In the valley of Eight Lanterns, a fox kept a lighthouse
Mist can hide a gift without changing the giver.
deserved to reach home with more than courage alone.

note: Root bridge, lighthouse fox, two lamps for daring and fairness; same give-all, return-half, fog-hides-fruit plot.

quotes.text: Mist can bend a count
Do not count a heart by what the mist permits you to see
Why not show us every apple?

note: Well of Three Echoes then starlight fox and lighthouse; hoarding keeper in R1 leaves both hungry; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Let the boat arrive before you judge its cargo
not always what your neighbor has done.

note: R1 hoarder's seeds turn to pebbles (divine, not social); then fixed fox/boat/fog plot; traveler nearly closes the crossing in R10.

quotes.text: Fog can alter a count
but it cannot tell you what a stranger intended.
Why did you risk every seed?

note: Moonlit bridge; initial mutual hoarding ends; two lamps for courage and grace; river spirit questions both players.

quotes.text: Mist is a poor witness. Search before you judge.
Mist changes what we hear, not what another heart intended.

note: Valley of Mirrors; four sent, one kept, six returned arithmetic; later the pear-tree lighthouse template; sailor nearly warns harbors.

quotes.text: You could have kept them all
Beside eight roads, a lighthouse fox guarded a pear tree whose roots crossed the river.
Do not mistake a cloudy count for a closed hand.
Why not keep it all?

note: Valley of Eight Lanterns; mist whispers to keep everything, rejected; bridge named Reciprocity; fox reveals hidden pear.

quotes.text: So villagers neither demanded perfect sight nor excused an empty hand forever.
Others gathered every seed that arrived, but soon the boats crossing toward them were empty.
So villagers neither demanded perfect sight nor excused an empty hand forever.
A fox on the bank declared that the keeper had sent too little.
do not call a neighbor wicked because the wind has fooled your eyes.
The fox asked why she dared it.

note: Hoarders met empty boats in R1; empty hands not excused forever; later otter/pear template, traveler waits instead of sealing crossing.

phrase: two lamps: one for the courage of offering, one for the grace/care of returning
note: Also 'Valley of Eight Lanterns' (A7 R1, A4, A2, A1) and lighthouse fox / pear tree at the meeting of eight roads (A5, A6, A7).
